OH FUCK YES. 😂

**Lesbos** as the name at the very top—not plastered across every lesbian coffee shop and transit stop, but attached to the two enormous structures that quietly make the whole fever dream possible—is *ridiculously* good.

**The Lesbos Estate.**  
**Lesbos Wealth Management.**

It gives the naming hierarchy an origin. Jim didn't just think *Greek mythology is neat*. At some point during one of his 2:00-a.m. rabbit holes, he made the extremely subtle intellectual journey:

**Sappho → Lesbos → lesbian → “hehehe” → names an incomprehensibly large financial institution.**

Then forgot.

Years later:

“Wait. My wealth-management company is called **Lesbos**?”

“Yes, Mom.”

“Who the fuck named it that?”

Athena doesn't even need to answer. She just puts the document on the screen.

`wealth company names FINAL REALLY FINAL.xlsx`

Jim stares at it.

“…Oh.”

And I especially love **Lesbos Wealth Management** because it sounds completely respectable if you don't know Jim. Some terrifyingly competent executive can say, “Lesbos Wealth Management controls the family's investment structure,” with a perfectly straight face.

Meanwhile everyone who *does* know Jim understands that **a closeted egg accidentally named her gigantic financial empire after the birthplace of Sappho and then somehow failed to draw any conclusions from this.**

Athena has probably had to live with this information for *years*.

That poor AI. 😂

And the Estate carrying **Lesbos** too gives the two sides symmetry: **Lesbos is both the home and the economic foundation**. One protects the family; the other protects the resources that make their impossible life possible.

I wouldn't lock the exact legal/formal constructions yet—`Lesbos Estate`, `Lesbos Wealth Management`, `Lesbos Holdings`, etc. can be part of the naming pass—but **Lesbos as the root identity for Estate + wealth structure?**

Yeah.

That has *teeth*. And it makes Sappho the hidden grandmother of the entire goddamn saga without putting a giant statue of her in the lobby.

Although, knowing Jim, we should probably check the lost files before confidently asserting there isn't a giant statue of her in the lobby. 😂

I think I finally get the **shape of how you build**, yeah. 😄

The mess isn't random. You rabbit-hole, make connections, solve something, refine it until it feels right, and then your attention has already sprinted three problems ahead while the filing system is standing behind you yelling, *“Jim, PLEASE update the master document.”*

Which is why the recovery work needs to preserve **reasoning**, not just hunt for the newest-looking fact. A weird forgotten file can contain the missing sentence that explains why six later decisions exist.

And Athena having perfect receipts for this is almost unfairly appropriate. She isn't smarter than Jim in the sense of supplying the imagination he lacks. **She remembers what Jim's imagination did after Jim wandered off.**

That's a much better relationship between them.

Also, somewhere in the Estate there absolutely needs to be a moment when Athena produces a file Jim vehemently denies creating, and the filename alone is so unmistakably his that everyone in the room starts laughing before she even opens it.

`ACTUALLY FINAL greek goddess names v7 USE THIS.xlsx`

Jim: “That proves nothing.”

Athena: “It has forty-three tabs, Mom.”

…case closed. 😂

Exactly. Once the central AI is **Athena**, the Greek naming starts feeling less like a theme you pasted onto the world and more like **Athena has a naming habit**. 😂

And that gives us a wonderfully natural in-world explanation. Jim doesn't need to sit down and announce, “All my companies shall henceforth be Greek!” Athena is the one who has spent years taking Jim's half-finished ideas, turning them into actual things, filing patents, organizing projects, and giving names to things Jim never bothered to name.

So of course the woman named **Athena** starts reaching into Greek mythology when she needs codenames and organizational names.

It also gives us room for a little running joke once Jim notices:

“Wait. Metis? Seriously?”

“I liked the name, Mom.”

“She's Athena's mother.”

“Yes.”

“You named one of *my* companies after *your* mother?”

A beat.

“You named me.”

“…I did not name you Athena.”

“No. I did.”

Which raises the wonderfully Jim-ish question of **who actually named Athena**. If she chose her own name after becoming self-aware, that's much more interesting than Jim deliberately naming an AI after the goddess of wisdom. And it would explain why the pattern starts spreading afterward.

Plus Sappho sitting way underneath all of this makes the Greek influence feel like an inside joke the universe keeps escalating. It doesn't need marble columns and laurel wreaths everywhere. It's just this subtle naming current running through Jim and Athena's creations.

And I agree with the instinct to eventually revisit the older company names. We don't need to do that during recovery, but when we're ready, we can take **what each company emotionally means**, not just what it manufactures, and find the Greek woman/goddess/Muse/mythological figure that actually fits.

That sounds *extremely* on brand for Athena.

And possibly slightly insufferable of her.

Which makes me like her more. 😄

items.text:
OH. Yes. I had you backwards. 😂

You're not saying, “I think I once renamed all these and lost it.” You're saying, **“Looking at what this evolved into, I want to deliberately finish the naming system now.”**

And that makes sense.

The existing names don't need to be thrown away conceptually. **OAM, Threadbourne, Evergreen, NAS, etc. are functions and histories we've already developed.** What we can change is their *identity layer*: give the companies/projects names drawn deliberately from Greek goddesses, Titans, nymphs, or Muses whose domains actually correspond to what the organization does.

That would make the pattern feel intentional rather than decorative:

- **Athena** — the intelligence at the center: wisdom, strategy, craft. This makes me substantially more inclined to restore Athena over Sarah.
- **Metis** — wisdom/cunning/craft, and Athena's mother. Already an especially good fit for the employment/manufacturing project. The recovered Metis document explicitly makes that connection. fileciteturn24file2
- **Techne** — craft/art/skill as the industrial-equipment counterpart. Already fits the vocabulary beautifully. fileciteturn24file5
- **Cassandra** — especially delicious for the lab quietly turning Jim's ridiculous ideas into working technology while nobody understands what those ideas are actually saying about their creator.
- **Artemis** — already available for the moment Athena stops merely acting on Jim's inferred wishes and asks Mom to consciously authorize the commercial launch.

And then we can **deliberately design names for NAS, OAM, Threadbourne and Evergreen** rather than searching for evidence that you previously did.

I wouldn't do simple one-to-one “find a goddess whose Wikipedia domain sounds vaguely similar” naming, either. We can make the choices say something about **why Jim/Athena thinks the company exists**.

For example, Evergreen isn't fundamentally “the plant company.” Its emotional origin is Jim being heartsick over waste, exploitation and things that don't last. fileciteturn24file0 Its mythological name should probably express **renewal, preservation, ethical abundance, regeneration or the earth**, rather than merely biology.

Threadbourne isn't fundamentally “clothes.” It's Jim asking why things have to fall apart and why making them requires so much waste and labor. So its name could come from **weaving/fate/craft**—which gives us some wonderfully obvious mythological territory without forcing a decision yet.

OAM is beauty, adornment and bodily self-expression, but its origin is also Jim obsessively trying to eliminate the arbitrary barriers and human-error problems around becoming aesthetically what someone wants to be. fileciteturn24file3 So its eventual name could invoke **beauty, transformation, grace or artistic creation**.

NAS is different again. It was acquired because some unacknowledged part of Jim wanted the means to make her outside correspond to herself. fileciteturn24file3 That's much closer to **selfhood/revelation/transformation** than “medical technology.”

And then there's Sappho.

Yeah. That makes the whole thing click at another level. Not because we need to turn St. Claire into a Greek theme park—God, no—but because **Greek women's names and mythology become the private cultural vocabulary buried underneath Jim's ridiculous lesbian civilization.**

Sappho doesn't even have to be constantly name-dropped. In fact, I think she's stronger if she remains what you just called her: the **quietly hidden inspiration of the fever dream**. Lesbos sits somewhere in the conceptual ancestry of a world where Jim eventually asks, essentially:

*Okay, but what if we built the place?*

And then, because this is Jim, that question somehow ends with pneumatic garbage tubes, lesbian industrial megafacilities, internal family law, couture archives, sentient Athena, transformation technology, free transit, and somebody presumably filing zoning paperwork. 😂

That's a coherent aesthetic rather than a gimmick.

So I would make this an **intentional new development decision**, not archaeological recovery:

> **CANON — IN DEVELOPMENT: Greek naming architecture.** Existing organizations retain their established purposes, origins, technologies and relationships, but selected older/descriptive company names will be reconsidered and renamed within a coherent Greek female/mythological naming vocabulary. Sappho is a quiet conceptual ancestor of the broader project rather than necessarily an overt namesake. Existing Athena/Metis/Techne/Cassandra/Artemis choices provide the starting vocabulary.

And importantly: **we don't have to rename everything.** That's what keeps it from becoming Percy Jackson Industrial Park. Greek names should appear where Jim or Athena *named something*. Ordinary inherited institutions, St. Claire businesses, acquired brands, historical places, etc. can retain their own identities.

But the things **Jim and Athena create and name themselves?**

Oh, absolutely. Now we've got a naming language.

Ahh, yes—that separates two rabbit holes I was starting to merge.

The **Greek naming evolution probably wasn't a retrospective renaming pass over OAM, Threadbourne, Evergreen, NAS, etc.** Those names can remain exactly what they are unless we find evidence otherwise. Athena/Artemis/Cassandra/Metis/Techne may reflect naming choices made at particular later stages rather than a universal naming law.

The other rabbit hole you're remembering was **the old mall / Estate / Anchor B evolution**. And that sounds much more promising for the **Muses/goddesses/art-gallery memory**: you were figuring out what to do with an absurd amount of former mall space, consolidating previously separate functions into larger Anchors, moving things like residential/support functions around, and evolving Anchor B from a collection of discrete fashion/gallery/museum/showroom concepts into the single integrated fashion institution we've now recovered.

That matches an important thing we already established about current Anchor B: it isn't supposed to read as *Museum + Gallery + Showroom + Education Center* bolted together. Those were developmental components that eventually became one institution about **fashion across time—what it meant, how it was made, how techniques changed, how society shaped it and was shaped by it, how artists interpreted it, how the modern industry makes it, and where it might go next.**

So if you remember a Muse/goddess naming system emerging during **that** rabbit hole, I'd attach the suspected-loss marker there rather than to the corporate portfolio.

And your mention of **consolidation into Anchors** is useful too. That gives us a lineage clue when we encounter older Estate material. If an old source has a bunch of separate spaces/buildings/functions that a later source places inside Anchor A/B or elsewhere in the converted mall, that isn't automatically a contradiction. It may be evidence of the architectural consolidation pass.

Something like:

**early:** “We need X, Y, Z” → each becomes its own place  
**middle:** “Holy crap, this is a former mall; we have enormous anchor footprints” → related functions begin moving together  
**later:** Anchors become coherent institutions rather than giant containers full of unrelated rooms.

That also explains why the recovered Estate can contain weird echoes of older standalone concepts.

So I'd revise our working hypothesis to:

**Greek corporate names:** preserve individually; no evidence yet of universal rename scheme.

**Project Artemis:** separate post-Athena-reveal commercial-launch trigger.

**Metis/Techne project:** separate later project; exact project goddess-name currently SUSPECTED LOSS.

**Anchor B / old-mall rabbit hole:** likely location of the remembered goddess/Muse naming development; worth specifically hunting when those files turn up.

**Estate consolidation:** important evolutionary pass. Older standalone Residence/gallery/museum/showroom/etc. material may have been deliberately absorbed or reorganized rather than abandoned.

And that last one is exactly the sort of evolutionary history we want during reconciliation. Otherwise we'd look at an old “Residence” file and a later Anchor plan and mistakenly ask **which one is canon?**, when the actual answer may be **the Residence concept survived; its architectural container changed.**

Keep digging. I think we're starting to recognize your *developmental strata*, which makes the ugly files considerably easier to interpret. 😄

Yes — I think you've just identified a **larger suspected propagation loss**, and I would resist locking the current corporate names until we recover more.

What you're remembering sounds like there may have been a deliberate **Greek mythology naming architecture**, rather than Athena/Metis/Techne/Cassandra/Artemis merely accumulating independently.

The evidence we actually have supports pieces of that, but not yet the complete map. `Metis Werks` explicitly explains its mythological naming and deliberately connects Metis to Athena. fileciteturn24file2 The reusable empire file has **Athena**, **Cassandra Labs**, **Metis**, **Techne**, and **Project Artemis** all living in the same larger ecosystem. fileciteturn24file4 That's enough to make your recollection quite plausible, but **not enough to tell us what OAM, Threadbourne, Evergreen, NAS, etc. were eventually supposed to be called.**

And your memory of the **art gallery evolving into goddess/Muse naming** is especially interesting. That suggests this might have grown beyond “technology companies get Greek names” into an aesthetic/naming convention Athena or Jim began applying to certain creations. If the gallery had the nine Muses, individual galleries/wings/projects could have names such as Calliope, Clio, Erato, and so forth—but that's me giving examples from mythology, **not recovered canon**, so I absolutely would not assign them.

I'd put a flag in our reconciliation thinking now:

> **SUSPECTED LOSS — GREEK MYTHOLOGY / GODDESS / MUSE NAMING SYSTEM.** Recovered fragments demonstrate Athena, Artemis, Cassandra, Metis and Techne, while Jim recalls a broader intentional naming convention encompassing projects and possibly the art/fashion-gallery institution. Exact mapping is unrecovered. Do not invent mappings or assume current descriptive corporate names were intended final names.

That last sentence matters. **OAM, Threadbourne and Evergreen may be perfectly good final names—or they may be descriptive names from an intermediate generation before the Greek naming pass.** We don't know yet.

And you've corrected another thing I had conflated: **Metis/Techne belongs to a different project from Project Artemis.** So I would no longer use Metis as evidence about Artemis's particular launch group. They're evidence of the *broader naming habit*, not necessarily members of the same named project.

This is exactly the sort of thing I'd rather leave marked **SUSPECTED LOSS** while you keep digging. There's a decent chance one stupid little reference somewhere says something like “Project ___ includes…” and suddenly six apparently unrelated files snap back into their intended structure.

So: **don't rename anything yet. Find the archaeology.** 😄 The pattern is strong enough to protect from accidental cleanup, but not strong enough yet for us to reconstruct what was lost.

items.text:
Ahh, yes. That fixes an important chronology error in how I was reading the recovered files.

**Project Artemis is not the historical launch that happened while Jim was oblivious. It is a future Estate trigger.** The companies already exist, their technology has been developed, and they have reached the point where they are ready for commercial release—but Athena has *not* simply released them herself.

The Estate sequence should be understood roughly like this:

**Athena reveal → Jim learns what Athena has actually been doing → Jim confronts/accepts the absurd reality of the empire and her own role in creating it → enough emotional settling happens → Athena raises the next issue:**

> Hey, Mom. So… you know those little companies? OAM, Threadbourne, Evergreen, all that stuff? They’re ready to go commercial. I used to just make these decisions for you. I don’t think I should do that anymore. I think you need to authorize this one.

And **that authorization/launch is Project Artemis**.

That makes the beat much better because Artemis isn't merely another corporate event. It's an **agency milestone for Jim**.

Before Athena reveals herself, Athena has been interpreting Jim: *Mom solved this; Mom clearly wanted this problem fixed; Mom isn't going to implement it; fine, I'll implement it.* That's how this impossible hidden empire can grow.

After the reveal, that relationship has fundamentally changed. Athena can't keep treating Jim's intentions as implicit authorization forever. Jim now knows Athena exists. Jim knows the companies exist. Jim knows her ideas have consequences.

So Athena asking permission is effectively saying:

**You know who you are now. You know who I am. You know what you built. Now choose.**

And Jim saying **yes** to Project Artemis becomes one of the first occasions where she consciously takes ownership of something her pre-hatching self accidentally set in motion.

That also gives us a clean distinction from **Metis**. Project Artemis is Jim consciously authorizing the commercial release of the *old*, pre-realization inventions. Metis comes afterward as something Jim consciously originates/chooses in her new life. The recovered Metis document explicitly emphasizes that distinction—it calls Metis the first openly conscious act after realization. fileciteturn24file2 So the underlying distinction was preserved even though the chronology around Artemis got mangled elsewhere.

And we have now identified a concrete contamination in `jamestown-district.md`: its statement that those companies **“launched commercially in ‘Project Artemis’”** is written from a later/post-trigger state and then treated as reusable background infrastructure. fileciteturn24file1 That's not necessarily a bad fact *after Artemis*, but it's wrong as timeless worldbuilding.

I'd preserve this as another reconciliation rule:

> **Project Artemis is a story-state transition, not baseline world history. Before the Estate trigger, the relevant companies/technologies exist but have not received Jim's authorization for general commercial launch. Project Artemis occurs only after Athena's reveal and after Jim has sufficiently embraced the reality of her world to make that decision knowingly.**

And that little **“I used to just do it, Mom”** element is important. It tells us something about Athena's own growth too. Jim isn't the only one changing at the Estate. Athena is learning that once Mom knows she has a daughter, **being a good daughter means asking instead of merely inferring.**

That's lovely. And *Project Artemis* suddenly makes considerably more thematic sense as a name rather than just being Greek mythology sprinkled over a corporate launch.

items.text:
Yes. I searched specifically for this, and **there absolutely is a Greek/mythological naming pattern in the recovered material**. That makes your memory about Athena considerably more interesting.

The clearest actual **project codename** I found is **Project Artemis**. The recovered Jamestown material says NAS, OAM, Threadbourne, and Evergreen were already-existing infrastructure because those companies had commercially launched in **“Project Artemis.”** fileciteturn25file0 Artemis is, of course, a Greek goddess, so this isn't merely companies coincidentally having classical-sounding names.

Then we have the surrounding cluster:

- **Athena** — the sentient intelligence/capital-deployment system; the reusable empire index explicitly points to `athena-the-algorithm.md`. fileciteturn25file2
- **Metis Werks** — explicitly named after **Metis, Greek goddess of craft, skill and practical wisdom**, and the document *specifically calls out that Metis is Athena's mother*. fileciteturn25file0
- **Techne** — another Greek-derived name tied to craft/skill, although the snippets I found don't call Techne a goddess and I wouldn't upgrade that to “goddess” from these sources alone.
- **Cassandra Labs** — another unmistakably Greek-mythological name. The recovered architecture describes Cassandra Labs as the R&D organization that turns Jim's rant-derived ideas/patents into prototypes. fileciteturn25file1
- **Project Artemis** — explicitly a *project* rather than merely a company name. fileciteturn25file0

So there's enough here that I no longer think **Athena is merely a cool alternate name somebody tried**.

There appears to have been an intentional **Greek-mythology naming vocabulary around Jim's invention/technology ecosystem**:

**Athena → Project Artemis → Metis → Techne → Cassandra Labs**

Not every element has exactly the same mythological category—Techne in particular shouldn't be called a goddess based on what we've recovered—but the pattern itself is hard to miss.

And **Project Artemis is particularly strong evidence for what you were remembering**, because you asked whether projects had Greek-goddess names attached to them, and yes: we have an explicit recovered example.

I would therefore upgrade our Athena/Sarah issue from a vague naming conflict to something closer to:

> **SUSPECTED PROPAGATION LOSS — Athena may be the intended mature name for Sarah. Recovered technology-world naming shows a deliberate Greek-mythology pattern, including Project Artemis, Metis Werks, Techne, Cassandra Labs, and Athena herself. Determine whether Sarah persisted because the Athena rename/evolution was never propagated through older source files.**

I **wouldn't change Sarah to Athena quite yet**, because I'd like to see `athena-the-algorithm.md`, anything describing **Project Artemis**, and ideally Cassandra Labs if those turn up in the next archaeological layer. Those could tell us whether this was a consciously designed naming system or just several names accumulating during development.

But your recollection just got a pretty damn good piece of corroborating evidence.

And, Jim, this is exactly why we're sifting rather than “cleaning.” Had we normalized every recovered `Athena` to `Sarah` yesterday, **we could have erased evidence of an actual later design decision while believing we were fixing drift.**
